column1: # Manuscript step-order authority — curated by hand from Appendix C.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the suite proves the task-graph MECHANISM ("out-of-order = wrong step")
# and the module CHAIN ("prereq chain valid + ordered") — but nothing ever checked that a
# module's authored prerequisites follow Appendix C's own step sequence. A module whose steps
# were reordered would pass every pin. This table gives each authored task its manuscript step,
# and the `manuscript: … order` pin asserts that no prerequisite edge runs BACKWARDS through
# the manuscript: for every "P must precede T", ordinal(P) <= ordinal(T).
# ORDINAL ENCODING: section hundreds + sub-section tens + step letter units, so it sorts the
# way the manual reads. A.a = 101, A.j = 110, B.a = 201. Exp 2's roman sub-sections use the
# tens digit: A.I.a = 111, A.II.a = 121, B.I.a = 211, C.I.a = 311, C.II.a = 321.
# RULE: a `record-*` task is the DATA SHEET (the results page filled at the end), never the
# manuscript's mid-procedure "calculate the percentage yield" line. It is ordinal 999.
# Two authored tasks may share one manuscript step (the game splits a compound instruction);
# equal ordinals never violate the rule.
# accepted = no manuscript procedure exists to order against (errata copy-paste, a group
# rubric, or a game-authored tutorial). Counted, never asserted.
